# Automated actions

The commands `mt help` lists under Automated actions. Automations are known as automated actions in Maitento, which is why these commands start with `action-`. More in [Automations](../../../concepts/automations.md).

In a terminal, type `mt` and then the command. In the interactive shell and the cloud shell, type the command on
its own. `mt help <command>` shows the same details in your terminal.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`action-create`](#action-create) | Create an automation from a JSON array of actions; add its schedules and triggers afterwards |
| [`action-delete`](#action-delete) | Delete an automation and its schedules and triggers, by `--name` or `--id` (at once, with no `--confirm`) |
| [`action-get`](#action-get) | Show an automation by `--name` or `--id`: how many schedules and triggers it has, and when it next runs |
| [`action-history`](#action-history) | List the runs an automation started, newest first: when, what triggered it, the outcome and any error |
| [`action-list`](#action-list) | List the automations in a namespace |
| [`action-msg-trigger-add`](#action-msg-trigger-add) | Add a message trigger to an automation: start it when an app, interaction or capsule run changes and matches a filter |
| [`action-msg-trigger-disable`](#action-msg-trigger-disable) | Switch off a message trigger of an automation, without removing it |
| [`action-msg-trigger-enable`](#action-msg-trigger-enable) | Switch a message trigger of an automation back on |
| [`action-msg-trigger-remove`](#action-msg-trigger-remove) | Remove a message trigger from an automation |
| [`action-msg-trigger-update`](#action-msg-trigger-update) | Change a message trigger of an automation: its name, type or filter (only what you give changes) |
| [`action-schedule-add`](#action-schedule-add) | Add a schedule to an automation: a cron expression in fields, in UTC (a field left out means every) |
| [`action-schedule-disable`](#action-schedule-disable) | Switch off a schedule of an automation, without removing it |
| [`action-schedule-enable`](#action-schedule-enable) | Switch a schedule of an automation back on |
| [`action-schedule-remove`](#action-schedule-remove) | Remove a schedule from an automation |
| [`action-schedule-update`](#action-schedule-update) | Change a schedule of an automation: its name or cron fields (only what you give changes) |
| [`action-trigger`](#action-trigger) | Run an automation now, without waiting for a schedule or trigger (prints the id of the first run it starts) |
| [`action-update`](#action-update) | Replace an automation's name, description and actions (its schedules and triggers are kept) |

## action-create

Create an automation from a JSON array of actions; add its schedules and triggers afterwards.

```text
mt action-create <name> [options]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<name>` | text | yes |  | The automation's name (unique in the namespace) |

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--description, -d <value>` | text |  |  | What the automation is for |
| `--actions, -a <value>` | text | yes |  | What it starts: a JSON array of actions, each a name and a config whose $type comes first (app, interaction, interaction-message, capsule or codepipeline) |

## action-delete

Delete an automation and its schedules and triggers, by `--name` or `--id` (at once, with no `--confirm`).

```text
mt action-delete [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--id`) |
| `--id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |

## action-get

Show an automation by `--name` or `--id`: how many schedules and triggers it has, and when it next runs.

```text
mt action-get [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--id`) |
| `--id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |

## action-history

List the runs an automation started, newest first: when, what triggered it, the outcome and any error.

```text
mt action-history [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--id`) |
| `--id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |
| `--limit, -l <number>` | whole number |  | `50` | Maximum number of entries to list (the history keeps the newest 50) |

## action-list

List the automations in a namespace.

```text

```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |

## action-msg-trigger-add

Add a message trigger to an automation: start it when an app, interaction or capsule run changes and matches a filter.

```text
mt action-msg-trigger-add [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--action-name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--action-id`) |
| `--action-id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |
| `--trigger-name, -tn <value>` | text |  |  | A name for the trigger |
| `--type, -t <value>` | text | yes |  | The kind of run whose changes it listens to: AppProcessUpdated, InteractionProcessUpdated or CapsuleProcessUpdated |
| `--filter, -f <value>` | text |  |  | A JSONPath filter over the change (the run is under item, its status a number): it fires only on a match; with none, on every change |
| `--enabled, -e` | flag |  |  | Whether the trigger fires (default: true; `--enabled` false adds it switched off) |

## action-msg-trigger-disable

Switch off a message trigger of an automation, without removing it.

```text
mt action-msg-trigger-disable [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--action-name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--action-id`) |
| `--action-id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |
| `--trigger-id, -t <id>` | id | yes |  | The trigger's id (action-msg-trigger-add prints it) |

## action-msg-trigger-update

Change a message trigger of an automation: its name, type or filter (only what you give changes).

```text
mt action-msg-trigger-update [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--action-name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--action-id`) |
| `--action-id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |
| `--trigger-id, -t <id>` | id | yes |  | The id of the trigger to change |
| `--trigger-name, -tn <value>` | text |  |  | A new name for the trigger |
| `--type <value>` | text |  |  | A new kind of run to listen to: AppProcessUpdated, InteractionProcessUpdated, CapsuleProcessUpdated |
| `--filter, -f <value>` | text |  |  | A new JSONPath filter ('none' removes it, and the trigger then fires on every change) |

## action-schedule-add

Add a schedule to an automation: a cron expression in fields, in UTC (a field left out means every).

```text
mt action-schedule-add [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--action-name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--action-id`) |
| `--action-id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |
| `--schedule-name, -sn <value>` | text |  |  | A name for the schedule |
| `--minute, -m <value>` | text |  | `*` | Cron minute field: 0-59, a list (0,30), a range (0-10) or a step (*/15) |
| `--hour, -hr <value>` | text |  | `*` | Cron hour field, in UTC: 0-23 (for example 7, or 9-17) |
| `--day-of-month, -dom <value>` | text |  | `*` | Cron day-of-month field: 1-31 |
| `--month, -mo <value>` | text |  | `*` | Cron month field: 1-12 or JAN-DEC |
| `--day-of-week, -dow <value>` | text |  | `*` | Cron day-of-week field: 0-6 (0 is Sunday) or SUN-SAT; 1-5 for weekdays |
| `--second, -s <value>` | text |  |  | Cron second field, 0-59, for a six-field expression (default: none, five fields) |
| `--enabled, -e` | flag |  |  | Whether the schedule runs the automation (default: true; `--enabled` false adds it switched off) |

## action-schedule-disable

Switch off a schedule of an automation, without removing it.

| `--action-id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |
| `--schedule-id, -s <id>` | id | yes |  | The schedule's id (action-schedule-add prints it) |

## action-schedule-update

```text

```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |

| `--day-of-month, -dom <value>` | text |  |  | A new cron day-of-month field: 1-31 |
| `--month, -mo <value>` | text |  |  | A new cron month field: 1-12 or JAN-DEC |

| `--second <value>` | text |  |  | A new cron second field, for a six-field expression ('none' goes back to five fields) |

## action-trigger

Run an automation now, without waiting for a schedule or trigger (prints the id of the first run it starts).

```text
mt action-trigger [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--name, -n <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's name, in the namespace (or give `--id`) |
| `--id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id, instead of its name |

## action-update

Replace an automation's name, description and actions (its schedules and triggers are kept).

```text
mt action-update [options]
```

| Option | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--namespace, -ns <value>` | text |  |  | The namespace to use (default: your default namespace; see ns-get) |
| `--id, -i <id>` | id |  |  | The automation's id (or give `--current-name`) |
| `--current-name, -c <value>` | text |  |  | The automation's current name, in the namespace, instead of `--id` |
| `--name, -n <value>` | text | yes |  | The automation's name from now on: a new one, or its current name to keep it |
| `--description, -d <value>` | text |  |  | What the automation is for (left out, the description is cleared) |
| `--actions, -a <value>` | text | yes |  | Every action it starts, replacing the old ones: a JSON array, as action-create takes it |
